newsitem.title: CHINA: China to invest $4.14 bln in railroads in 1997.
newsitem.headline: China to invest $4.14 bln in railroads in 1997.

text.p: China will increase investment in railroad development by 2.4 billion ($289 million) in 1997 to help exploit natural resources in remote regions and spur development in backward areas, the China Daily said on Tuesday.

The Ministry of Railways will boost spending to 34.4 billion yuan ($4.14 billion) yuan, an increase of about 6.9 percent from last year, to lay 1,269 km (788 miles) of track and build 1,750 km (1,087 miles) of electrified railway, the newspaper said.
The funds would also be used to open 1,261 km (784 miles) of new railway and 444 km (276 miles) of rail on secondary lines, it quoted vice-minister Cai Qinghua as saying.

Beijing would pour another 2.65 billion yuan into finishing work on the Beijing-Kowloon line that opened last year and 1.5 billion yuan would be spent to lay a line from Xi'an to Ankang in coal-rich northern Shaanxi province, Cai said.
Other projects would link Shaanxi's major coal mining base of Datong with the eastern port of Qinhuangdao, he said.
Another 1.4 billion yuan would go to the Nanjiang Railway in the south of the northwestern region of Xinjiang, he said. The line would help development of the area's oil resources.

Rail authorities would spend 5.8 billion yuan on a 900-km (560 mile) electrified line linking Nanning in the mountainous southwestern region of Guangxi with Kunming in neighbouring Yunnan province, he said but gave no further details.
